title: Infra GPU Fleet Capacity, Cloud Accounts, Networking, IaC & CI/CD Playbook - Ops Guide Addendum
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This addendum consolidates operational guidance for GPU fleet capacity, cloud accounts and networking, Terraform/IaC modules, and CI/CD pipelines. It is intended for on-call engineers, infra SREs, and platform owners who run Redwood's inference capacity. The doc prioritizes pragmatic, tested procedures, conservative thresholds, and validated Terraform/CI patterns.

Scope

- GPU fleet capacity planning and autoscaling thresholds for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Cloud account structure and networking constraints required for Private/VPC deployments.
- Terraform module usage and recommended module inputs/outputs.
- CI/CD pipeline patterns for IaC and runtime deployments.
- Runbook procedures for common incidents affecting capacity and networking.

Owner and Contacts

- Primary owner: infra-platform (engineering) - Aisha Patel (author)
- On-call escalation: infra-sre rotation (PagerDuty: infra-sre)
- Module maintainers: @miguel-torres (terraform), @elena-chen (networking)

Definitions and Services

- gpu-pool-service: logical service name for managed GPU pools that serve inference workloads.
- infra-ci: GitHub Actions org pipeline for IaC validation and apply.
- redwood-network-controller: central VPC and peering controller for Private deployments.
- instance types: h100-80gb, a100-40gb, a10g-24gb (preferred ordering: h100 > a100 > a10g for new pools).

SLOs and Operational Targets

- Median tail latency for token generation (p95): <= 200ms for standard models on Dedicated pools.
- GPU utilization target (steady state): 60-75% per-GPU. Sustained >85% for more than 10 minutes requires capacity increment or throttling.
- Autoscaling reaction time: scale-up within 3 minutes (triggered by queue length), scale-down cooldown 15 minutes.
- Allocation failure rate (Terraform apply error causing capacity shortfall): <1% over rolling 7-day windows.

Capacity Planning Guidance

1) Forecast inputs
   - QPS by model, median sequence length, tokens-per-request.
   - Expected concurrency and burst headroom (default 2x peak QPS).
   - Reservation vs on-demand split: aim 70% reserved for predictable workloads.

2) Working formula (simple):
   - tokens_per_sec_per_gpu = GPU_throughput(model_profile) / average_token_latency
   - required_gpus = ceil(expected_tokens_per_sec / tokens_per_sec_per_gpu * safety_factor)

3) Safety factors and thresholds
   - Safety factor default: 1.25 for production pools, 1.5 for pre-prod.
   - Minimum pool size: 4 GPUs.
   - Max single-pool % of region capacity: 25% to avoid noisy-neighbor risks.

Terraform / IaC Modules (Recommended patterns)

- Modules (canonical names):
  - redwood/gpu-pool (versioned): creates ASG/VMSS or GKE node pool, attaches GPU drivers, configures taints/labels.
  - redwood/network-vpc: VPC, subnets, routing, transit gateways, peering and shared services.
  - redwood/cloud-accounts: org-level IAM bindings, billing exports, logging config.
  - redwood/iam-roles: service accounts and role-bindings for controllers.

Module input examples (YAML-like snippets inside string):

  # example use of redwood/gpu-pool
  module "gpu_pool_inference_prod" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@repo/redwood/terraform-modules.git//gpu-pool?ref=v1.12.0"
    region = "us-west-2"
    instance_type = "h100-80gb"
    gpu_count = 8
    min_size = 4
    max_size = 64
    autoscaler = true
    labels = { role = "inference", env = "prod", pool = "dedicated-001" }
  }

Recommended module outputs (to wire into CI/CD automation): pool_id, vpc_id, subnet_ids, kube_node_group_name, iam_role_arn.

Terraform best practices

- Remote state: use state locking (e.g., S3 + DynamoDB for AWS).
- Workspaces: per-environment with naming convention redwood-{env}-{region}.
- Run plan + apply limited to module targets for incremental changes.
- Mandatory pre-apply checks: plan approval by 2 infra reviewers for prod.

CI/CD Patterns for IaC and GPU Runtime

- Branching: trunk-based with short-lived feature branches. Merges to main trigger infra-ci/plan workflow.
- Pipeline stages (infra-ci): lint -> terraform init -> terraform plan -> plan artifact -> human approval (prod) -> terraform apply.
- Automated validation steps post-apply: smoke test deployments, node readiness, driver and nv_peer_memory checks.
- Runtime deploy pipeline (runtime-ci): build inference container -> push image -> rolling deploy to pool via controller API -> post-deploy traffic shift (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%).

Snippet: GitHub Actions job names and required secrets

- infra-ci workflow: .github/workflows/infra-ci.yml
  jobs:
    plan:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - name: Terraform Init
          run: terraform init -backend-config="bucket=${{ secrets.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}"

Required secrets: TF_STATE_BUCKET, TF_STATE_DYNAMODB_TABLE, CLOUD_ACCOUNT_SA, CLOUD_API_KEY, SSH_DEPLOY_KEY.

Networking and Cloud Account Requirements

- Account structure: billing org account (shared), infra account per-cloud-region, customer private accounts for Private deployments.
- VPC layout: 3 private subnets per AZ, dedicated subnet per GPU pool, transit gateway attachments for cross-account networking.
- Network policies: deny-by-default egress rules between customer workloads; allow only control-plane egress to redwood-core endpoints (control-plane.redwood.internal).
- Peering and DNS: use shared Route 53 inbound/outbound delegation for private hosted zones; prefix internal names with "redwood-".

Minimum networking sizing table:

| Component | Minimum CIDR | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| VPC | /20 | Supports ~4090 IPs; recommended for multi-pool clusters |
| GPU pool subnet | /24 per AZ | Allows up to 250 nodes; increase for larger pools |
| Private hosted zone | N/A | Name: internal.redwood.local |

Runbook: Common Incidents and Actions

1) Incident: Pool OOM / GPU OOM errors increasing (symptom: repeated job restarts, high evictions)
   - Triage: check gpu-pool-service metrics: OOM count, pod eviction rate, GPU memory utilization.
   - Quick mitigation: scale up pool by 25% or reduce per-request concurrency via rate-limiter.
   - Permanent fix: adjust autoscaler thresholds and review model memory profiles; consider model quantization profile.

2) Incident: Unexpected allocation failures during Terraform apply (e.g., quota exhausted)
   - Triage: inspect cloud account quotas, recent changes to reserved capacity, and provider API errors in apply logs.
   - Quick mitigation: rollback to last known good module target or incrementally apply smaller changes.
   - Long-term: automate quota checks in infra-ci and gate large-scale applies with quota approval ticket.

3) Incident: Network partition between control-plane and GPU pools
   - Triage: confirm VPC route tables, peering status, and firewall/security group changes.
   - Quick mitigation: failover traffic to alternate region pool (policy-driven), open emergency access to control-plane CIDR.
   - Postmortem: capture change that introduced partition, tighten change approval for network rules.

Change and Release Process

- All production Terraform changes require:
  1) CI plan approval by two infra reviewers.
  2) Smoke test in staging region.
  3) Rolling apply with canary for stateful pools (apply to a single AZ/pool slice first).
  4) 30-minute observation window with health checks (GPU utilization, p95 latency, error rate).

Validation and Testing

- Pre-merge unit tests: terraform validate and tflint.
- Integration test: infra-ci runs a staged apply to a throwaway test account and runs kube node/productivity checks.
- Performance test: run microbenchmarks using benchmarking-and-perf-suite (locally or in infra-perf account) with representative model profiles.

Ownership and Escalation Matrix

- gpu-pool infra owner: infra-platform team (primary on-call).
- Networking and VPC: infra-networking (second-level).
- Terraform modules: infra-modules guild (module owners listed in module READMEs).
- Escalation: on-call -> module owner -> infra-eng director -> CISO (for security-sensitive incidents).

Appendix A: Example Terraform check command

- Example: run from feature branch before PR
  export TF_VAR_region=us-west-2
  terraform init -backend-config="bucket=${TF_STATE_BUCKET}"
  terraform plan -var='env=staging' -target=module.gpu_pool_inference_prod

Appendix B: Quick CLI validation for GPU nodes (SSH into node or use remote exec)

- Check nvidia-smi and driver versions:
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total,memory.free,driver_version --format=csv
- Check MIG and nv_peer_memory as needed:
  lsmod | grep nv_peer_memory || true
